title: Harmony instance (HarmonyLib.Harmony)
text: The entry point. Create one per mod with a unique id (reverse-DNS, e.g. 'archdukejim.mymod'). Call PatchAll() to apply every annotated patch class in the assembly, or Patch(...) to patch a single method. The id namespaces your patches so UnpatchAll(id) removes only yours.

title: PatchAll
text: Scans an assembly for classes marked with [HarmonyPatch] and applies their prefix/postfix/transpiler/finalizer methods. No-arg PatchAll() scans the calling assembly. This is the usual way mods apply patches at startup.

title: Manual Patch()
signature: harmony.Patch(MethodBase original, HarmonyMethod prefix=null, postfix=null, transpiler=null, finalizer=null)
text: Patch one method imperatively, without annotations. Wrap your patch methods in HarmonyMethod. Returns the generated replacement MethodInfo. Use this when the target is computed at runtime (generics, private methods found via AccessTools) rather than known at compile time.

title: HarmonyMethod
signature: new HarmonyMethod(MethodInfo method, int priority=-1, string[] before=null, string[] after=null)
text: Wraps a patch MethodInfo plus its metadata (priority, before, after) for manual Patch() calls. new HarmonyMethod(typeof(MyPatch), nameof(MyPatch.Prefix)) is a common shorthand.

title: AccessTools
text: Reflection helper toolkit. Finds and caches MethodInfo/FieldInfo/PropertyInfo/constructors ignoring access modifiers, plus utilities like TypeByName, FieldRefAccess, MakeDeepCopy, Inner (nested types). Prefer it over raw System.Reflection — it handles inherited members and binding flags correctly.

title: AccessTools.Method
signature: AccessTools.Method(Type type, string name, Type[] parameters=null, Type[] generics=null); AccessTools.Method("Namespace.Type:Method")
text: Resolve a MethodInfo including private/static, with optional parameter-type array to pick an overload and generics to close a generic method. The string form 'Verse.GenSpawn:Spawn' avoids a typeof reference. Returns null if not found — check it before patching.

title: AccessTools.Field / FieldRefAccess
text: Field(type,name) returns a FieldInfo for any field. FieldRefAccess<T,F> returns a fast ref-returning delegate to read/write a private instance field without reflection overhead each call — ideal in hot paths. StaticFieldRefAccess handles static fields.

title: AccessTools property helpers
text: Return the get_/set_ MethodInfo of a property so you can patch or invoke it. To patch a property with attributes, use [HarmonyPatch(typeof(T), "Prop", MethodType.Getter)] instead.

title: Traverse
text: Fluent reflection navigator for reading/writing private fields and calling private methods at runtime: Traverse.Create(obj).Field("name").SetValue(v); Traverse.Create(type).Method("M", args).GetValue<T>(). Slower than FieldRefAccess but convenient for one-off access and chaining.

title: PatchProcessor
text: Low-level programmatic patching: create a processor for a method, AddPrefix/AddPostfix/AddTranspiler with HarmonyMethods, then Patch(). Also PatchProcessor.GetPatchInfo(method) inspects who else has patched a method — useful for diagnosing conflicts.

title: Harmony.DEBUG / FileLog
text: Set Harmony.DEBUG = true BEFORE patching to dump generated IL and patch decisions to a harmony.log.txt on the Desktop (via FileLog). Essential for debugging transpilers and 'my patch isn't firing' problems. Turn it off in release.

title: Unpatch / UnpatchAll
text: Remove patches. UnpatchAll(id) removes only patches tagged with your id (safe); UnpatchAll() with no id removes ALL Harmony patches from every mod (almost never what you want). Rarely needed in RimWorld since mods patch once at startup.

title: [HarmonyPatch] targeting
text: Marks a class as a patch and names the target. Forms: typeof + method name; string 'Namespace.Type' + method for types you can't reference; class-level [HarmonyPatch(typeof(Class))] combined with method-level [HarmonyPatch("Method")]; use nameof(Class.Method) for refactor-safety.

title: Disambiguating overloads
text: When the target method is overloaded, pass a Type[] of the exact parameter types so Harmony picks the right one. For ref/out params use new Type[]{ typeof(int).MakeByRefType() } with [HarmonyArgument] as needed. Ambiguous match without this throws at patch time.

title: Patching properties / constructors
text: MethodType selects Getter/Setter for properties, Constructor for .ctor, and Normal for methods. For an indexer or the [] getter use MethodType.Getter with the parameter types. Constructor patches see the instance via __instance in a postfix (it exists by then).

title: [HarmonyPrefix]
text: Runs before the original. Return void to always continue, or bool: false skips the original method (and later prefixes) — postfixes still run. Set ref __result before returning false to supply the result. Inject __instance, args by name, ___privateFields, __state.

title: [HarmonyPostfix]
text: Runs after the original. Read or modify the return value via ref __result, or use the pass-through form static T Postfix(T __result){...return __result;}. Always runs (even when a prefix skipped the original), so it's the safest place to observe/adjust results.

title: [HarmonyTranspiler]
text: Rewrites the original method's IL. Receives the instruction stream (optionally ILGenerator generator and MethodBase original) and yields the modified stream. The most powerful and most fragile patch type — use CodeMatcher and match on stable anchors, not absolute offsets.

title: [HarmonyFinalizer]
text: Wraps the original in a try/finally. Inject Exception __exception (null if none thrown). Return null to swallow the exception, or return an Exception to replace/rethrow it. Use for cleanup and for making a crashing vanilla method non-fatal.

title: [HarmonyReversePatch]
text: Copies the original method's IL into a stub you declare, so you can call original (even private) logic directly, or call the un-patched original bypassing other mods' patches. HarmonyReversePatchType.Original copies the pristine method; Snapshot copies the currently-patched version.

title: Priority / Before / After
text: Order patches from different mods on the same method. Priority values: Last(0), VeryLow(100), Low(200), LowerThanNormal(300), Normal(400 default), HigherThanNormal(500), High(600), VeryHigh(700), First(800). Before/After name other Harmony ids to sequence relative to them. Only meaningful when multiple patches share a target.

title: [HarmonyTargetMethod] / [HarmonyTargetMethods]
text: When the target can't be expressed as an attribute (computed generic instantiation, a private nested method, or several methods), a static TargetMethod() returning a MethodBase — or TargetMethods() returning IEnumerable<MethodBase> — supplies it. Build the MethodBase with AccessTools.

title: [HarmonyArgument]
text: Rename or index-map an injected original argument when your parameter name differs, or select an argument by position: [HarmonyArgument(0)]. Needed when the original's parameter name is unknown or clashes with an injection name.

title: [HarmonyPatchCategory]
text: Tag patch classes with a category and apply only that group via harmony.PatchCategory(name) instead of PatchAll(). Lets a mod enable/disable sets of patches conditionally (e.g. only when another mod is present).

title: [HarmonyDelegate]
text: Generates a fast delegate that calls a private/internal method, as an alternative to reflection or a reverse patch for repeated invocation.

title: __instance
text: Injects the object the method was called on (the 'this'). Type it as the declaring type. Absent/irrelevant for static targets. In a constructor postfix it is the freshly-built instance.

title: __result
text: The original method's return value. Read it in a postfix; modify it with ref (or via the pass-through form returning the same type). In a prefix, set ref __result and return false to override the return without running the original. Its type MUST equal the original's return type.

title: __state
text: A scratch value passed from prefix to postfix for the same call. Prefix sets it (out/ref); postfix reads it. Use it to capture a before-value (e.g. a stat before the original changes it) and compare after, or to stash whether the prefix decided to skip.

title: __args
text: All original arguments as an object[]; writing back into it (with ref object[] __args) changes what the original receives. Prefer named parameters for type safety; use __args for generic/variadic patch code.

title: ___privateField (triple underscore)
text: Injects a private field of the target instance by name, prefixed with three underscores. Add ref to write it. Cleaner than reflection for reading/writing internal state from a patch. For static private fields the same syntax works.

title: __0, __1, ... (arg by index)
text: Access the original's arguments positionally when you don't know their names. __0 is the first parameter. Use ref to modify. Equivalent to [HarmonyArgument(0)].

title: Original argument by name
text: A patch parameter whose name and type match one of the original's parameters is injected with that argument's value. Add ref to change what the original sees (prefix) or observe it (postfix). This is the most readable way to read call arguments.

title: __originalMethod
text: Injects the MethodBase of the method being patched — useful when one patch method targets many methods (via TargetMethods) and needs to know which one is running.

title: __exception (finalizer only)
text: In a finalizer, the exception the original (or a prior patch) threw, or null. Return null to swallow it, or return an Exception to replace what propagates. The only place __exception is available.

title: __runOriginal (Harmony 2.2+)
text: A read-only bool telling a prefix whether the original will still run given earlier prefixes' skip decisions, and telling a postfix whether the original actually ran. Lets cooperating patches avoid double work. You cannot set it to force-run.

title: Prefix semantics
text: Prefixes run in priority order before the original. A void prefix always lets execution continue. A bool prefix returning false skips the original AND all later prefixes; returning true continues. Postfixes and finalizers still run after a skip. Use a prefix to validate/short-circuit or to mutate incoming args by ref.

title: Postfix semantics
text: Postfixes run after the original in reverse-priority order. Read/modify ref __result, read args and __state, or use the pass-through form (static T Postfix(T __result, ...)) which reads and returns the result. Because postfixes always run, they're the reliable place to adjust outputs; avoid heavy work in hot methods.

title: Postfixing an IEnumerable (yield) method
text: To add/remove/replace items a method yields, take and return the IEnumerable in a postfix: foreach over __result yielding items, then yield your extras. This is how you inject extra float-menu options, gizmos, recipes, etc. Don't ToList() unnecessarily — keep it lazy.

title: Finalizer semantics
text: Finalizers wrap the original like try/finally and run even on exception. Injecting Exception __exception lets you inspect it; returning null swallows it, returning an Exception replaces it. Two finalizers can chain. Use to harden a fragile vanilla method so one mod's bad data doesn't crash the game.

title: Transpiler semantics
text: A transpiler transforms the original's CIL before it is JIT-compiled: it receives IEnumerable<CodeInstruction> and returns the edited sequence. It runs once at patch time, not per call, so it's zero-overhead but brittle across game updates. Match on stable operands/anchors, keep edits minimal, and enable Harmony.DEBUG to verify the emitted IL.

title: Patch ordering across mods
text: When several patches target one method, order is: prefixes by priority high→low (Before/After adjust relative to named ids), then the original, then postfixes low→high. Transpilers chain in priority order, each seeing the previous one's output. Ordering only matters between patches that interact; design patches to be order-independent when you can.

title: CodeInstruction
text: A single IL instruction (opcode + operand) plus labels/blocks, the unit transpilers manipulate. Helpers: CodeInstruction.Call(type,name,params) emits a call; .LoadField/.StoreField; clone with new CodeInstruction(instr). Preserve existing labels when replacing an instruction or jumps break.

title: CodeMatcher
text: The robust way to write transpilers (Harmony 2.x). A cursor over the instruction list: MatchForward/MatchBack to anchors (CodeMatch on opcode/operand), then Insert/SetInstruction/RemoveInstructions/Advance, and InstructionEnumeration() to emit. Use ThrowIfInvalid so a failed match fails loudly instead of silently no-op'ing.

title: Transpilers helpers
text: Transpilers.MethodReplacer swaps every call to one method for another across the stream — a clean way to redirect a call without hand-writing IL. Transpilers.EmitDelegate inlines a delegate as IL so you can splice C# logic mid-method. Both are far safer than manual opcode surgery.

title: RimWorld: apply patches at startup
signature: [StaticConstructorOnStartup] static class Boot { static Boot(){ new Harmony("id").PatchAll(); } }
text: The vanilla RimWorld pattern: a [StaticConstructorOnStartup] class whose static constructor creates a Harmony instance and calls PatchAll(). Runs once after defs load. Alternatively patch from your Mod subclass constructor (this toolkit's ToolkitMod does exactly that). Do it once, early, before the targets are called.

title: RimWorld: patch from the Mod constructor
signature: public class MyMod : Mod { public MyMod(ModContentPack c):base(c){ new Harmony("id").PatchAll(); } }
text: If your mod has a Verse.Mod subclass (for settings), its constructor is a natural place to PatchAll(). Harmony is guaranteed loaded by then because your About.xml lists brrainz.harmony as a dependency loaded first. Pair with LongEventHandler.ExecuteWhenFinished for work needing defs.

title: Patch a computed/generic/private target
text: When the method to patch isn't known at compile time — a closed generic, a compiler-generated iterator/lambda, or a private overload — use [HarmonyTargetMethod] (or TargetMethods for several) returning a MethodBase built with AccessTools.Method(...). For iterator internals, resolve the nested MoveNext via AccessTools.EnumeratorMoveNext / the generated type.

title: Conditionally replace a return value
signature: static bool Prefix(ref bool __result, Pawn pawn){ if(cond){ __result=false; return false; } return true; }
text: Override a method's result only in some cases: in a prefix, when your condition holds set ref __result and return false to skip the original; otherwise return true to run it normally. Cleaner and more compatible than a transpiler for simple gating.

title: Attach data to instances you don't own
text: To store extra per-instance state on a vanilla type you can't modify, use a ConditionalWeakTable<TInstance,TData> keyed by the instance (auto-frees with GC), or __state for within-a-single-call data. In RimWorld, a mapped GameComponent/WorldComponent or a Def-based comp is usually the savable option; the weak table is for transient runtime data.

title: Call a private method/original logic
text: To invoke a private method: a [HarmonyReversePatch] stub (fastest, IL-copied), a [HarmonyDelegate], AccessTools.Method(...).Invoke(obj,args) (simplest), or Traverse.Create(obj).Method(name,args).GetValue(). Reverse patch also lets you call the ORIGINAL past other mods' patches.

title: Harmony vs HarmonyLib namespace
text: Harmony 1.x lived in namespace 'Harmony' with a HarmonyInstance class; Harmony 2.x (what RimWorld 1.1+ uses) lives in namespace 'HarmonyLib' with the Harmony class. Copy-pasted 1.x snippets won't compile — change 'using Harmony;' to 'using HarmonyLib;' and 'HarmonyInstance.Create(id)' to 'new Harmony(id)'.

title: 'Could not resolve type HarmonyLib.Harmony'
text: This runtime error means the 0Harmony assembly wasn't loaded before your mod. In RimWorld: list brrainz.harmony in About.xml <modDependencies> and load it FIRST. In this toolkit's isolated (Steam-bypassed) launch, Harmony lives only in the Steam Workshop, so it vanishes unless Steam is signed in or the Workshop mod is mirrored into local Mods/ — the launcher warns about this. Never ship your own 0Harmony.dll.

title: JIT inlining defeats patches
text: The runtime may inline very small methods (trivial getters, one-liners) so a patch on them never fires — the call site was replaced with the inlined body. Signs: prefix/postfix silently never runs though the patch applied. Workarounds: patch the CALLER instead, or transpile the caller. RimWorld's Mono is less aggressive than .NET Core but it still happens.

title: __result type must match
text: __result must be declared as the original method's exact return type (use ref to modify). A mismatch (e.g. int __result on a method returning float, or wrong for a void method which has no __result) fails the patch at apply time or throws. For void methods there is no __result.

title: Patching generic methods/types
text: You patch a CLOSED generic method (a specific T), not the open definition. Use AccessTools.Method(type, name, null, new[]{ typeof(T) }) to close it, supplied via [HarmonyTargetMethod]. Patching one instantiation doesn't patch the others. Generic type methods likewise need the closed declaring type.

title: A skipping prefix affects other mods
text: When your bool prefix returns false it skips the original for everyone, and other mods' later prefixes too — a common source of cross-mod incompatibility. Prefer a postfix or a narrowly-scoped transpiler when you don't truly need to prevent the original. If you must skip, use high priority deliberately and document it.

title: Don't bundle 0Harmony.dll
text: In RimWorld, Harmony is provided by the brrainz.harmony mod; shipping your own 0Harmony.dll in Assemblies/ causes version clashes and 'multiple Harmony' chaos. Reference 0Harmony with <Private>false</Private> so it's compile-time only, and depend on the Harmony mod at runtime.

title: Use nameof for method/field names
text: String method names in [HarmonyPatch(..., "Method")] silently break when the game updates and renames or removes the member — the patch just stops applying. Prefer nameof(Class.Method) where the member is public so a rename becomes a compile error. For private members that nameof can't reach, keep the string but verify against the current API dump.

title: Patch before the target runs
text: Apply patches at startup (static ctor or Mod ctor), not lazily, so no un-patched call slips through first. Transpilers must be in place before the method is first JITed. Don't patch inside a hot path or repeatedly — patch once.

title: RimWorld Harmony dependency & load order
text: Harmony is the mod 'Harmony' by brrainz (packageId brrainz.harmony, Workshop 2009463077). Declare it in About.xml <modDependencies> and put it above your mod in <loadAfter>/load order so 0Harmony is loaded first. RimWorld ships no Harmony itself — every C# mod that patches depends on this one.

title: Patch vs Def vs override
text: Reach for Harmony only when XML defs/PatchOperations and normal subclassing (ThingComp, HediffComp, custom Def/Verb/JobDriver classes) can't do the job. Patching is for changing existing hardcoded behavior; new content should be defs + comp classes, which are more compatible and save-friendly.

title: Harmony 2.0 (major rewrite)
text: 2.0 was a ground-up rewrite: namespace moved to HarmonyLib, the Harmony class replaced HarmonyInstance, a redesigned annotation API, a MonoMod-based IL backend, introduction of FINALIZERS as a fourth patch type, and CodeMatcher for transpilers. RimWorld adopted Harmony 2 around game version 1.1.

title: Harmony 2.1–2.3 highlights
text: Later 2.x releases added broader runtime support (newer .NET/Mono), the __runOriginal injection (2.2) so cooperating patches can tell whether the original will/did run, reverse-patch and CodeMatcher improvements, and many stability fixes. Check the source below for exact per-version notes before relying on a specific feature.

title: Harmony release notes & docs (source of truth)
text: Authoritative sources: release notes at https://github.com/pardeike/Harmony/releases and the manual at https://harmony.pardeike.net . This corpus is a curated summary for fast retrieval — when a version detail matters, confirm against those pages (rebuild_harmony_corpus can ingest an updated data file).
